clos.original_description: Students will develop a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts and principles of text mining, including techniques for extracting, transforming, and analyzing textual data.
clos.enriched_description: Develop a solid understanding of text mining principles for extracting, transforming, and analyzing textual data. The scope includes regular expressions, text normalization, edit distance, n-gram language models, smoothing and Kneser-Ney smoothing, perplexity and entropy, Naive Bayes, logistic regression, vector semantics, TF-IDF, Word2Vec, clustering, topic modeling, RNN/LSTM models, transformers, masked language models, machine translation, dialogue systems, parsing, relation and event extraction, temporal reasoning, WordNet, word-sense disambiguation, and sentiment or affect lexicons.

clos.original_description: Students can use machine learning/deep learning (neural networks, neural language models, recurrent neural networks, LSMT) for specific text-mining applications.
clos.enriched_description: Use machine learning and deep learning methods for text-mining applications. The scope includes Naive Bayes text classification and sentiment analysis, precision, recall and F-measure, cross-validation and statistical significance testing, logistic and multinomial logistic regression, cross-entropy loss, gradient descent, regularization, RNNs, LSTMs, attention, transformers, pretrained language models, masked language models, and fine-tuning.

clos.original_description: Students will explore the methods and algorithms used for text classification and clustering tasks. They will learn to apply techniques like Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, and k-means clustering.
clos.enriched_description: Explore methods and algorithms for text classification and clustering. The CLO itself names Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, and k-means clustering, while the mapped topics emphasize unsupervised text clustering, document similarity, and topic modeling.

clos.original_description: Students will learn about different methods for representing text data, such as bag-of-words, term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF), and word embeddings. They will understand the strengths and limitations of each approach.
clos.enriched_description: Learn methods for representing text data and understand their strengths and limitations. The scope includes lexical and vector semantics, word vectors, cosine similarity, TF-IDF, pointwise mutual information, Word2Vec, embedding visualization and evaluation, bias in embeddings, context-free and dependency parsing representations, logical sentence meaning, WordNet, word-sense disambiguation, word-sense induction, and sentiment or affect lexicons.

clos.original_description: Students will be aware of the popular applications in text mining, such as machine translation, question answering, and chatbots to design text mining-related applications in real-world
clos.enriched_description: Be aware of popular text mining applications and design text-mining-related applications for real-world contexts. The scope includes machine translation with encoder-decoder models, low-resource translation, machine translation evaluation, bias and ethical issues, chatbot and dialogue-system properties, simple frame-based dialogue systems, dialogue-state architecture, dialogue system evaluation, and dialogue system design.
